follow100Note: Rows reconcile to $100 at this rounding; the $28M other operating income credit sits inside 'Other income' — see the footer note.
footerNote: Business units are shown as originally reported for fiscal 2024 — Compute and Networking, Storage, Mobile, and Embedded (Q3 FY24 Form 10-Q segment note; operating margins are from that note, as Micron reported no gross margin by unit that quarter) — because no SEC filing reports this quarter on the recast structure Micron adopted in fiscal 2026 (Cloud Memory, Core Data Center, Mobile and Client, Automotive and Embedded). The reorganization took effect in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 (FY25 Form 10-K, Note 27), and the Q3 FY25 earnings release contains no business-unit table; on the recast basis Micron has filed only full-year FY24 unit revenue (FY25 10-K: Cloud Memory $3,792M, Core Data Center $4,984M, Mobile and Client $11,667M, Automotive and Embedded $4,631M, All other $37M) and the FQ4-24 quarter (Q4 FY25 earnings release), so no quarterly recast split of FQ3-24 exists. Reported operating income was $719M; Micron's $28M 'Other operating (income) expense, net' line was income this quarter, so the chart shows it in the other-income step rather than as a negative expense — chart operating income is therefore $691M, $28M below the reported figure, with net income unchanged at $332M.

oneTimers: The GAAP tax bill was unusually heavy — a $377M provision on $715M of pre-tax income (about 53%); Micron's non-GAAP reconciliation includes $150M of estimated tax effects and other tax adjustments, a large part of the gap between GAAP net income of $332M and non-GAAP net income of $702M (which also excludes $217M of stock-based compensation).
There were no restructure and asset-impairment charges this quarter (versus $68M a year ago) and no inventory write-down charge — a clean quarter after the glut-era charges of fiscal 2023.
otherDetail: Interest income of $136M on Micron's cash pile, less $150M of interest expense, plus $10M of other non-operating income and the $28M net other operating income credit described in the footer — a net +$24M in this step; equity-method investments lost a further $6M, shown in their own step.

segments.name: Compute and Networking
segments.note: Memory for client PCs, cloud and enterprise servers, graphics and networking — the unit where HBM for AI servers sits; revenue rose 18% sequentially on data-center DRAM pricing, at a 17% operating margin this quarter ($442M of operating income).

segments.name: Mobile
segments.note: Memory and storage for smartphones and other mobile devices — at a 19% operating margin this quarter ($301M of operating income), the highest of the four units.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Memory and storage for cars, industrial and consumer markets — revenue rose 16% sequentially on automotive demand, at a 10% operating margin this quarter ($124M of operating income).

segments.name: Storage
segments.note: SSDs and component storage for enterprise and cloud, client and consumer markets — revenue jumped 50% sequentially on data-center NAND demand and record data-center SSD sales, at a 6% operating margin ($76M of operating income).

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Small residual outside the four business units, so the units sum to total revenue.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $6.81B from $3.75B a year ago and beat Micron's guidance, as AI demand drove data-center revenue up 50% in a single quarter to a record share of the mix — with share gains in high-bandwidth memory and record data-center SSD revenue.
takeaways.title: AI demand ignites data center

takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 26.9%, up from -17.8% a year ago when a memory glut forced write-downs — and reported operating income was $719M, versus a $1,761M operating loss in the same quarter last year.
takeaways.title: Margins swung from red to green

takeaways.text: Net income was $332M ($0.30 a share) versus a $1,896M loss a year ago. A $377M tax provision on just $715M of pre-tax income held GAAP profit well below the $702M non-GAAP figure ($0.62 a share).
takeaways.title: Profit again — after a heavy tax bill

verdict: Micron's revenue rose 82% in a year to $6.81B as AI demand lit up data-center memory — gross margin swung from -18% to 27%, and the company earned $332M after losing $1.9B in the same quarter a year earlier, even after a $377M tax bill.
